nodes.statement: Fix binary intervention Q, latent structural pole Z, two marker channels M1/M2 and ordered consequence Y; actual bearer, interval, complete signature, route installation/use, target and measurement remain distinct sorts.
nodes.scope: 256 deterministic binary SCM parameterizations; not a complete organization or actual-token admission.
nodes.quantifier: For every assignment of the eight declared structural-equation bits.

nodes.statement: Under each do(Q=q), observe M1=Z XOR s1, M2=Z XOR s2 and Y=y(Z,q) with Z=z(q).
nodes.scope: Both binary Q values within the R195 domain.
nodes.quantifier: For each model and q in {0,1}.

nodes.statement: Complementing Z and both marker signs while conjugating the Y kernel preserves every declared do(Q) observation; 256 models form 128 fixed-point-free pairs.
nodes.scope: The deterministic binary R195 model class.
nodes.quantifier: For every model in R195:DOMAIN and both declared interventions.

nodes.statement: Route sensitivity and a prospectively reversed marker can establish intervention-relative causal structure while retaining global latent-pole complement symmetry.
nodes.scope: The route-sensitive and reversed-marker subset of the R195 model class.
nodes.quantifier: For every model satisfying z(0)!=z(1) and s1!=s2.

nodes.statement: An explicit ordered-outcome bridge such as Y=Z orients the latent pole relative to Y; its complement is the opposite bridge Y=1-Z.
nodes.scope: Complete consequence-table restrictions in the finite domain.
nodes.quantifier: For every model satisfying the declared full-table bridge.

nodes.statement: A separate prospective premise must justify why the functionally oriented pole is the positive familiar-mineness pole rather than merely success, reward, protection or low-error polarity.
nodes.scope: The selected familiar embodied/action-mineness target, not basal experience.
nodes.quantifier: For every proposed transfer from an ordered consequence to F_fam.

nodes.statement: A substantive interventional anchor jointly requires target declaration, same-instance actuality, ontic intervention, installed use, functional direction, phenomenal direction transfer, reliability/rival control and a defeater.
nodes.quantifier: For every proposed interventional polarity anchor.

nodes.statement: A declared intervention and positive test are evidence about an actual route; they do not install the route, prove its same-episode use or define experience structure.
nodes.scope: One bound body/action protocol absent separately discharged physical and measurement premises.

nodes.statement: Use interventions to identify causal or functional orientation, then independently audit phenomenal direction transfer, actuality, use, reliability and token admission before naming familiar mineness.
nodes.scope: UCT bodily/action self-experience research; no basal gate, unique owner or assistant-consciousness verdict.
nodes.quantifier: For every future named-target application using interventions.

rules.statement: Apply the explicit complement/conjugation transform and compare both do(Q) observation tables.
rules.binding: The variable sorts, intervention family, observation channels and structural-equation class remain fixed across each model pair.
rules.alternative_route_semantics: An asymmetric target-directed restriction is outside the complement-closed class rather than an alternative proof route.

rules.statement: Restrict to route-sensitive and reversed-marker models and retain the complement pairing.
rules.binding: Both restrictions are imposed on the same model and both interventions.
rules.alternative_route_semantics: A functional anchor is treated by a different rule and adds a directional premise.

rules.statement: Add the full-table directional relation Y=Z and show its complement is Y=1-Z.
rules.binding: The complete Y ordering and Y-to-Z relation are fixed prospectively on one model domain.
rules.alternative_route_semantics: Other ordered consequences orient only relative to their separately declared semantics.

rules.statement: Expose rather than discharge the independent premise linking functional outcome polarity to F_fam.
rules.binding: The structural pole, ordered consequence and selected experiential target remain different sorts on one proposed application.
rules.alternative_route_semantics: Opposite target interpretations preserve all structural and outcome facts until independent phenomenal evidence is added.

rules.statement: Combine the causal result and open semantic premise into an eight-field prospective adequacy contract.
rules.binding: All fields concern one bearer, interval, signature, route, intervention and target; none is borrowed from a different experiment.
rules.alternative_route_semantics: Missing phenomenal direction transfer yields functional orientation only; missing actuality yields a model/test result only.

rules.statement: Place interventional orientation inside the existing coordinate-transport/semantic-residual architecture without gating basal experience.
rules.binding: Any positive UCT application must retain one actual P/I/K binding and all R157 parameter-transport premises simultaneously.
rules.alternative_route_semantics: No individual premise establishes actual application or B_fam.

context_links.statement: R195 uses C1 only conditionally and neither proves nor replaces it.
Intervention, success, familiar mineness, report and self-model are not conditions for basal experience.
An oriented transported coordinate still does not acquire a phenomenal name without a bridge.
Present intervention tables do not manufacture actual same-lineage history or current consumer use.
The positive F_fam pole remains an independently justified application target.
